topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection

outline.topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 min)
sections.content: Define a discrete signal as a sequence of numbers (e.g., pixel intensities). Explain the concept of a 'sliding window' or 'kernel' as a tool to transform a target pixel based on its neighbors.
sections.example: Imagine a 3x3 grid of pixels representing a tiny part of a cat's face; we want to calculate the average brightness to smooth the image.

sections.title: The Mechanism of Convolution (1.5 min)
sections.content: Define discrete convolution mathematically as the weighted sum of input elements within a kernel. Use visual animation showing a kernel flipping, sliding across an input matrix, and performing element-wise multiplication followed by summation.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Blurring Kernel' (all values 1/9) sliding over an image, replacing the center pixel with the average of its 8 neighbors.

sections.title: The Power of Kernels (1.5 min)
sections.content: Demonstrate how changing kernel weights produces different effects. Explain that convolution is essentially a filter that extracts specific patterns from signals or data structures.
sections.example: Contrast two kernels: a 'Blur' kernel (averaging) versus an 'Edge Detection' kernel (Sobel filter) that highlights the silhouette of a bird against the sky.

sections.title: Real-world Applications (1 min)
sections.content: Summarize how convolutions are the foundation of modern computer vision, specifically in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Conclude with how they process layers of visual data to recognize complex objects.
sections.example: A smartphone camera app: The device automatically applies a convolution filter to sharpen your selfie or detect faces by recognizing the high-contrast edges of eyes and mouths.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 min)
lecture_lines: Discrete signals are sequences of values like pixel intensities.
We use a kernel as a sliding window tool.
Kernels transform target pixels based on their neighbors.
Imagine a grid representing part of a cat.
We calculate average brightness to smooth the image.
animations: Display a 3x3 grid of discrete numeric pixel values in #FFFFFF.
Highlight a 3x3 kernel sliding window frame in #FFD700 over the grid.
Show kernel values transforming adjacent pixel values dynamically.
Visualize a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png] feature extraction area on a 5x5 grid.
Display a smoothing calculation showing output as average brightness value representing the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png].

storyboard.title: The Mechanism of Convolution (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Convolution is a weighted sum of kernel elements.
First, the kernel slides across the input matrix.
We perform element-wise multiplication for every step.
Next, we sum those values for the output.
This process generates a new, transformed signal.
animations: Display an input matrix [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/matrix.svg] next to a kernel matrix [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/kernel.svg] in #FFFFFF.
Animate the kernel [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/kernel.svg] sliding across the input matrix.
Show element-wise multiplication of overlapping matrix cells in #00FFFF.
Sum the resulting products to create a single output pixel value.
Show a new output matrix growing as the process continues to populate the pixel [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] grid.

storyboard.title: The Power of Kernels (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Different kernels produce unique effects on signals.
A blurring kernel averages neighboring pixel values.
An edge detection kernel highlights sharp transitions.
This extracts specific patterns from the data.
Convolutions act as flexible filters for processing.
animations: Display a grid and apply a blurring kernel in #FF00FF using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lens.svg].
Display a grid and apply an edge detection kernel in #00FF00.
Animate edge highlights appearing around a shape in the grid.
Show patterns like lines and curves being isolated using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/paintbrush.svg].
Represent convolutional filters as a versatile bank of tools using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/filter.svg].

storyboard.title: Real-world Applications (1 min)
lecture_lines: Convolutions are the foundation of computer vision.
They enable CNNs to recognize complex objects.
Apps use them to sharpen images automatically.
